# dlartg

> Generates a plane rotation (real Givens rotation).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlartg from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlartg';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlartg( f, g, c, s, r ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `number` | First component of the vector to be rotated |
| `g` | `number` | Second component of the vector to be rotated |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `c` |
| `s` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `s` |
| `r` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `r` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `f`: The first component of vector to be rotated.
- `g`: The second component of vector to be rotated.
- `c`: The cosine of the rotation.
- `s`: The sine of the rotation.
- `r`: The nonzero component of the rotated vector.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlartg.strided( f, g, c, s, r ) → void
```

Generates a plane rotation with real cosine and real sine, using alternative indexing semantics.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `number` | First component of the vector to be rotated |
| `g` | `number` | Second component of the vector to be rotated |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `c` |
| `s` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `s` |
| `r` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `r` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `f`: The first component of vector to be rotated.
- `g`: The second component of vector to be rotated.
- `c`: The cosine of the rotation.
- `s`: The sine of the rotation.
- `r`: The nonzero component of the rotated vector.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlartg()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARTG`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlartg.f90).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlartg from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlartg';

// Using the standard interface:
const c = new Float64Array( 1 );
const s = new Float64Array( 1 );
const r = new Float64Array( 1 );

dlartg( 1, 1, c, s, r );
let out = new Float64Array( [ c[ 0 ], s[ 0 ], r[ 0 ] ] );
console.log( out );

// Using the strided interface:
dlartg.strided( 1, 1, c, s, r );
out = new Float64Array( [ c[ 0 ], s[ 0 ], r[ 0 ] ] );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARTG`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLARTG generates a plane rotation so that

$$
\begin{bmatrix} C & S \\ -S & C \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} F \\ G \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} R \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}
$$

where $C^2 + S^2 = 1$.

The mathematical formulas used for C and S are

$$
R = \operatorname{sign}(F) \, \sqrt{F^2 + G^2}
$$

$$
C = F / R
$$

$$
S = G / R
$$

Hence $C \ge 0$. The algorithm used to compute these quantities incorporates scaling to avoid overflow or underflow in computing the square root of the sum of squares.

This version is discontinuous in R at $F = 0$ but it returns the same C and S as ZLARTG for complex inputs (F,0) and (G,0).

This is a more accurate version of the BLAS1 routine DROTG, with the following other differences:

-   F and G are unchanged on return.
-   If $G=0$, then $C=1$ and $S=0$.
-   If $F=0$ and (G .ne. 0), then $C=0$ and $S=\operatorname{sign}(1,G)$ without doing any floating point operations (saves work in DBDSQR when there are zeros on the diagonal).

Below, wp=\>dp stands for double precision from LA\_CONSTANTS module.

### Further Details

Anderson E. (2017) Algorithm 978: Safe Scaling in the Level 1 BLAS ACM Trans Math Softw 44:1--28 https://doi.org/10.1145/3061665

</section>
